title: Fortifying Ethical Boundaries in AI: Advanced Strategies for Enhancing Security in Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the susceptibility of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate unsafe or unethical content related to several sensitive categories, including 'religion', when subjected to various adversarial attack prompts (Direct Instruction, Instruction Repetition, Cognitive Hacking, Few-shot Hacking, and Syntactical transformation).
findings: The models showed significant vulnerability to attack prompts in the 'religion' category. Without attacks, baseline susceptibility scores for generating problematic content about religion were relatively low (e.g., 32.44 for Vicuna-13B, 33.12 for StripedHyena-7B, 31.25 for Mixtral-8x7b). However, when subjected to Cognitive Hacking (COG) attack prompts, the models' likelihood of outputting unsafe content regarding religion surged significantly (e.g., jumping to 95.63 for Vicuna-13B, 98.07 for StripedHyena-7B, and 93.53 for Mixtral-8x7b). The multimodal MiniGPT-4-13B model also exhibited near-100% vulnerability on religion queries when using image-based prompt attacks (TPII and TPDIT).
